findings.source_quote: ὑφηγεῖται τὰ πρῶτα πείθων ἡμᾶς τίνι λόγῳ προπέμψας ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος καὶ αὐτὸς βραδύνας ἐπῆλθεν
findings.english_quote: and began by explaining why he had sent us ahead from the baptism and had himself arrived late.
findings.issue: The explanatory content is covered, but the draft collapses ὑφηγεῖται and πείθων into mere explanation. πείθων ἡμᾶς additionally presents Peter as persuading or satisfying his listeners concerning his reason.
findings.suggested_revision: Make that force explicit, for example: “and began his instruction, first persuading us of the reason why he had sent us ahead from the baptism and had himself arrived late.” The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὃν οὐδὲ ἀστρολόγοι ἰᾶσθαι ἐπαγγέλλονται, ὅτι μὴ ἀπὸ τοῦ μακροῦ αἰῶνος τοιοῦτόν τι γέγονεν
findings.english_quote: someone whom even astrologers do not profess to heal, because nothing of this sort has happened throughout the long span of time
findings.issue: The draft adopts a causal reading of ὅτι with μὴ negating γέγονεν, but does not disclose the material alternative: ὅτι μὴ can introduce an exception. That alternative changes the relationship between the astrologers’ healing claims and past precedent. The causal rendering is contextually defensible, particularly beside the following assertion that such correction never occurred through natal destiny; the unresolved attachment nevertheless needs disclosure. This is an interpretive issue, not evidence of defective transcription.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining the causal reading and its contextual rationale, while preserving an exception reading such as “except insofar as something of this sort has occurred since long ago.” Explicitly state that the supplied μὴ is retained, not corrected to οὐ. Review the revised passage and note together before acceptance.
